text.p: Italian bond futures held firmer but were off the day's best levels supported by other bond markets and the strong lira, but activity was subdued ahead of CPI inflation data later this week, dealers said.
"The market is very quiet watching other bond markets and the slightly firmer lira. The next focus is the inflation figures on Thursday and Friday," said one LIFFE trader.

Dealers said that activity tended to be generally subdued throughout the day with many investors winding down for the christmas holiday or cautious ahead of the CPI numbers which might prompt a cut in interest rates.

Dealers said preliminary data from ten Italian cities on Thursday and Friday was likely to see Italian CPI inflation held at November's 2.6 percent rate in December, while Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi added Tuesday that he saw Italian inflation levelling out at November's 2.6 percent level.
There are still hopes that the CPI inflation data for December would prompt Italy's central bank into its third cut in interest rates this year, they added.
Italian Oct producer prices rose 0.4 percent year-on-year and Oct wholesale prices increased 2.1 pct annually. Both were in line with forecasts and had little overall market impact.

Most bond markets took some support after the U.S. Federal Reserve, as expected, held U.S. rates steady after a regular FOMC meeting late Tuesday. This came after Treasuries were hit by strong U.S. housing data for November.

On the domestic front, Italy's centre-left government won another confidence vote in the upper house Senate over the 1997 budget bill and the whole package might be fully ratified by the upper house late Wednesday, and then the draft law returns to the lower house for final approval.
